material_facts.description: Patient sustained a left arm crush/entrapment injury in industrial machinery on 2024-01-08, requiring on-scene tourniquet application and machine dismantling to free the arm.

Initial evaluation found complete mechanical disruption of the left arm/hand with bone protrusion, cold pulseless hand, and complete brachial artery and nerve transection with massive soft tissue loss.
The left upper extremity was determined to be unsalvageable due to complete vascular and neurologic disruption, with associated traumatic shock from blood loss.

Emergent left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation was performed on 2024-01-08, including brachial artery ligation, traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves, humeral sectioning, and myofascial closure.
Patient required PRBC transfusion (2 units) and IV fluid resuscitation intraoperatively/postoperatively for blood loss, followed by ICU admission for postoperative monitoring.
Imaging confirmed comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture with open segmental forearm/hand fractures and carpal disorganization.
Postoperative pain management included transition from IV PCA Dilaudid/morphine to oral oxycodone and escalating doses of gabapentin for phantom limb and neuropathic pain from January through 2025.
Patient developed severe phantom limb pain (rated 8/10) and stump hypersensitivity with radiating pain following amputation, which failed conservative management.
A post-amputation traumatic neuroma of the ulnar/median nerve terminals (measuring approximately 1.8 x 1.4 cm) developed at the stump, identified on 2024-06-18.
On 2024-11-12, patient underwent left stump neuroma excision with proximal resection of the median and ulnar nerves and transposition/embedding into the triceps muscle.
A neuroma revision procedure was performed on 2025-02-05 in conjunction with fitting of a custom myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis.
Patient underwent stump desensitization therapy and shrinker sock fitting beginning February 2024 to address phantom pain and hypersensitivity.

Patient completed an extended physical/occupational therapy and prosthetic training program from January 2025 through June 2026, including myoelectric prosthesis training, electrode calibration, grasping drills, and bilateral coordination/fine motor tasks.

Patient had physical/occupational therapy cancelled in December 2024 and multiple documented no-shows for therapy in May 2025 and November 2025, with a later lapse attributed to holiday workload and transportation issues.
Patient exhibited reduced left shoulder range of motion and decreased shoulder strength during 2025 PT evaluation, with shoulder fatigue occurring after only 15 minutes of prosthesis use.

Patient completed a comprehensive rehabilitation program and final functional capacity evaluation by June 2026, achieving near-normal left shoulder active range of motion and was discharged to return to modified light/medium duty work.
Patient had a prior left shoulder injury from a 2022 motorcycle fall diagnosed as AC joint sprain and mild rotator cuff tendinitis, treated with physical therapy and work restrictions.
CT angiography and X-ray of the left upper extremity on the date of injury confirmed complete brachial artery disruption and comminuted fractures supporting the unsalvageable limb determination.
Patient received prophylactic antibiotics (Cefazolin/Ancef, Cefdinir) and wound cultures during the initial hospitalization to manage infection risk from the open crush injury.
Following amputation, patient was fitted with and trained on a custom myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis to restore upper extremity function.
